evidence: Ov. Ars 1.476: dūra tamen mollī saxa cavantur aquā
Hor. S. 2.4.18: gallīna … dūra, a tough chicken
terms.comment: Hard to the touch, and tough to chew; the opposite is mollis (see soft). Hard to do is difficilis (see difficult). Of a person, dūrus is harsh: in mē dūrus, hard on me (Traupman 100).

phrases.latin: quid magis est saxō dūrum, quid mollius undā? dūra tamen mollī saxa cavantur aquā
phrases.english: what is harder than stone, what softer than water? And yet hard stones are hollowed out by soft water

phrases.latin: nē gallīna malum respōnset dūra palātō
phrases.english: so that a tough chicken doesn’t disagree with his palate

sources: Lewis & Short: durus
